newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Arafat appoints Hamas man sports minister.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat appoints Hamas man sports minister.

text.p: President Yasser Arafat swore in a leading figure from the militant Hamas Islamic group in Hebron as the Palestinian Authority's minister of youth and sports on Friday, witnesses and Palestinian sources said.
The move came a week after the Authority took control of 80 percent of Hebron -- a Hamas stronghold in the West Bank -- from Israel.
The new minister, Talal Sider, told Reuters: "I currently represent myself but I have many followers in Islamic political circles."

Sider's appointment marked a step in Arafat's efforts to ensure Hamas, officially opposed to interim peace deals with Israel as sellouts of the Palestinian cause, kept the peace in Hebron, long a flashpoint of Arab-Jewish violence.

The new minister, the only one in Arafat's cabinet associated with Hamas, was among some 400 Hamas supporters Israel deported to Lebanon in December 1992. The deportees were returned within a year after international pressure was brought to bear on Israel.

Some 400 Jews live in heavily fortified enclaves in the midst of Hebron's 100,000 Palestinians. Israeli troops still control the heart of the town, where the settlers live along with 20,000 Palestinians.

Hamas has spearheaded violent opposition to the peace deals. It shook the peace process to its foundations last February and March with a series of four suicide bombings over nine days that killed 59 people in Israel. Arafat has tried to get the group to express its opposition politically rather than through violence.
